Synopsis:
Dialog when interactin with the shrine dedicated to Mystra in Stormshore Tabernacle. All players will be able to read some lore about the god. Additionally, if the player is a cleric of Mystra they'll be able to give offerings and pray/communicate with the god to get a blessing.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_StormshoreTabernacle_MystraShrine.json: You are standing at the Mystra altar inside the Stormshore Tabernacle; every visitor can read an inscription giving basic lore about Mystra as the Mother of All Magic and a jealous patron of spellcasters. A Religion or similar knowledge check can unlock extra lore — failing it yields only the basic inscription. If the player is a cleric/follower of Mystra, additional interaction options appear to offer donations and pray, and those actions can elicit a blessing or a narrator cue that Mystra is attentive. A companion (Gale, in the examples) is present and uneasy about lingering at the shrine, commenting on catching Mystra’s eye.
- LOW_StormshoreTabernacle_SeluneShrine.json: You are standing before an altar to Selûne in the Stormshore Tabernacle; an inscription on the altar can be read by anyone and gives a short prayer about Selûne’s changing light and guidance. All characters will see the basic lore line identifying Selûne as the moon-and-stars goddess who helps wanderers. Characters with relevant scholarship in Religion (or who pass the associated check) will gain a bit more contextual knowledge; without that skill they get only the limited inscription text. If the player is a cleric/follower of Selûne, the goddess may acknowledge them (the “Moonmaiden welcomes you”), and they can offer gifts, pray, and receive a blessing.
- LOW_StormshoreTabernacle_TyrShrine.json: Dialog when interactin with the shrine dedicated to Tyrin Stormshore Tabernacle. All players will be able to read some lore about the god. Additionally, if the player is a cleric of Tyr they'll be able to give offerings and pray/communicate with the god to get a blessing.
- LOW_StormshoreTabernacle_HelmShrine.json: You are standing at the Helm shrine inside the Stormshore Tabernacle; every visitor can read an inscription describing Helm as a vigilant guardian and the nature of his worship. A Religion check or similar knowledge skill may gate additional lore — failing it yields only the basic inscription text. If the player is a cleric of Helm (i.e., a faithful follower), extra interaction options appear to offer donations and pray, and those actions can elicit a blessing or a narrator cue that Helm’s gaze welcomes the faithful. The shrine’s behavior and options mirror the general pattern used for other deity altars in the tabernacle (for example, the Selune shrine).
- LOW_StormshoreTabernacle_GenericShrine.json: Dialog with shrine where player can give blessings to gods that do not have their onw statue in Stormshore Tabernacle. Narratively we can say that that money will be spent on getting those gods a space of their own, or another well-intentioned purpose.Only one god will be on the dialog at the same time. And no one will be if a non-cleric character interacts with the shrine and begin the dialog.

- Narrator: *You see an altar dedicated to Mystra.* (node 24)
- Gale: Whatever you want with this idol, I'd prefer we make it quick. I'm not sure I'm comfortable catching Mystra's eye, even if it is made of stone. (node 13)
- Player: Read the words inscribed on the altar. (node 11)
- Narrator: *Mystra, Mother of All Magic, is the patron of wizards, and often called upon by other spellcasters as well. She's said to be a jealous goddess.* (node 15)
- : True (node 4)
- Narrator: *Even though you do not follow her, you feel her power resonating from the statue. She is the One True Spell at the heart of all spells. The Weave could not be in better hands.* (node 30)

context: You are standing before Mystra’s altar inside the Stormshore Tabernacle; an inscription visible to all names her the Mother of All Magic and a jealous patron of spellcasters. Any character can read the basic lore, while a successful Religion (or similar) knowledge check reveals additional background; failing that check yields only the limited inscription or a note that your studies don’t suffice. If the player is a cleric or follower of Mystra, extra options to give offerings and pray appear and those actions can grant a blessing or a narrator cue that Mystra is attentive. Even non‑followers may feel the goddess’s power resonating from the statue. Gale is present and uneasy about lingering at the shrine, warning about catching Mystra’s eye.
